results.title: Timoshenko's question on equally distributed elements (Kourovka 19.94)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for every natural number $n$ and all words $w_1, w_2$ in the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$, the words $w_1$ and $w_2$ have the same distribution if and only if some automorphism of the free metabelian group $M_n = F_n / F_n''$ maps the image of $w_1$ in $M_n$ to the image of $w_2$.

results.title: Equally distributed elements need not be automorphic (Kourovka 19.94)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: It is not the case that for every natural number $n$ and all words $w_1, w_2$ in the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$, the words $w_1$ and $w_2$ have the same distribution if and only if some automorphism of the free metabelian group $M_n = F_n / F_n''$ maps the image of $w_1$ in $M_n$ to the image of $w_2$.

results.title: Unique lift of a monic factor through a nilpotent-kernel surjection
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A monic factor of a coprime factorization lifts uniquely through a surjective homomorphism with nilpotent kernel. The original polynomial and the complementary reduced factor are not required to be monic.

results.title: Hensel lifting of coprime monic factors over a complete ring
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Coprime monic factors lift over a ring complete at the kernel of a surjective homomorphism. The lifts are coprime, and the first is the unique monic divisor of the original polynomial with its specified reduction.

results.title: Hensel's lemma for complete discrete valuation rings
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ that is complete and Hausdorff for the $\mathfrak{m}$-adic topology. Let $f \in A[X]$ have derivative $f'$, and let $a_0 \in A$ satisfy $f(a_0) \in \mathfrak{m}$ with $f'(a_0)$ a unit of $A$. Then $f$ has a root $a \in A$ with $a - a_0 \in \mathfrak{m}$.

results.title: Polynomials do not decrease the valuation of differences
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with normalized additive valuation $v \colon A \to \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$. For every polynomial $p \in A[X]$ and all $a, a_0 \in A$, we have $v(a - a_0) \le v(p(a) - p(a_0))$.

results.title: Nearby roots share the derivative valuation
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Uniqueness of roots near a point
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with normalized additive valuation $v \colon A \to \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, let $f \in A[X]$ have derivative $f'$, and let $a_0 \in A$. If $a, a' \in A$ are roots of $f$ with $v(f'(a_0)) < v(a - a_0)$ and $v(f'(a_0)) < v(a' - a_0)$, then $a = a'$.

results.title: Elements of the maximal ideal have positive valuation

results.title: Fuel-bounded generalized Hofstadter recursion
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $k$, $p$ and $n$, the value $A_k(p, n)$ is defined by recursion on the fuel $p$, which bounds the recursion depth: $A_k(0, n) = 0$ and $A_k(p + 1, n) = n - g^k(n - 1)$, where $g^k$ is the $k$-fold iterate of the function $g(m) = A_k(p, m)$ and both subtractions are truncated at $0$.

results.title: Generalized Hofstadter function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $k$, the function $F_k : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is given by $F_k(0) = 0$ and $F_k(n) = n - F_k^k(n - 1)$ for $n \ge 1$, where $F_k^k$ is the $k$-fold iterate of $F_k$ (the identity when $k = 0$).

results.title: The fuel-bounded Hofstadter recursion is bounded by its argument
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $k$, $p$ and $n$, the fuel-bounded value $A_k(p, n)$ of the generalized Hofstadter recursion satisfies $A_k(p, n) \le n$.

results.title: The generalized Hofstadter functions vanish at zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $k$, the generalized Hofstadter function $F_k$ satisfies $F_k(0) = 0$.

results.title: Recursion for the generalized Hofstadter function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $k \ge 0$ and every $n \ge 1$, the generalized Hofstadter function $F_k$ satisfies $F_k(n) = n - F_k^k(n - 1)$, where $F_k^k$ is the $k$-fold iterate of $F_k$.

results.title: First values of Hofstadter's G and H
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F_k$ denote the generalized Hofstadter functions. For $n = 0, 1, \dots, 10$ the values $F_2(n)$ are $0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 6$ and the values $F_3(n)$ are $0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6, 7$.

results.title: The Hofstadter substitution on letters
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $k$, the substitution $\tau_k$ sends the letter $k$ to the word $k\,1$ and every other letter $i \in \mathbb{N}$ to the one-letter word $i + 1$.

results.title: The Hofstadter substitution on finite words
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $k$, $\tau_k$ maps a finite word $w$ over $\mathbb{N}$ to the concatenation, in order, of the words $\tau_k(a)$ for the letters $a$ of $w$, where $\tau_k(k) = k\,1$ and $\tau_k(i) = i + 1$ for every letter $i \ne k$.

results.title: Letter images under the generalized Hofstadter substitution are nonempty
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $k$, let $\tau_k$ be the substitution on letters in $\mathbb{N}$ sending $k$ to the two-letter word $k\,1$ and every other letter $m$ to the one-letter word $m + 1$. For every natural number $i$, the image $\tau_k(i)$ of the letter $i$ has length at least $1$.

results.title: The generalized Hofstadter substitution does not shorten words
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $k$, let $\tau_k$ be the substitution on letters in $\mathbb{N}$ sending $k$ to the two-letter word $k\,1$ and every other letter $i$ to the one-letter word $i + 1$. For every finite word $w$ over $\mathbb{N}$, the word $\tau_k(w)$, obtained by replacing each letter of $w$ by its image under $\tau_k$, is at least as long as $w$: $|w| \le |\tau_k(w)|$.

results.title: The Hofstadter substitution preserves prefixes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a natural number $k$, let $\tau_k$ be the morphism of finite words over $\mathbb{N}$ that replaces the letter $k$ by the word $k\,1$ and every other letter $i$ by $i + 1$. For every $k$ and all finite words $u$, $v$ over $\mathbb{N}$, if $u$ is a prefix of $v$, then $\tau_k(u)$ is a prefix of $\tau_k(v)$.

results.title: Every iterate $\tau_k^j(k)$ starts with $k$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\tau_k$ be the substitution sending the letter $k$ to $k\,1$ and every other letter $i$ to $i + 1$, extended letterwise to words. For all natural numbers $k$ and $j$, the word $\tau_k^j(k)$, obtained by applying $\tau_k$ to the one-letter word $k$ a total of $j$ times, has the form $k\,r$ for some word $r$.

results.title: Consecutive iterates of the Hofstadter substitution on $k$ are nested

results.title: Bounded growth of a word under $\tau_k$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\tau_k$ be the substitution sending the letter $k$ to $k\,1$ and every other letter $i$ to $i + 1$, extended letterwise to words. Given $n$, a bound $f$ and a word $w$, the result is $w$ if $f = 0$ or $w$ has more than $n$ letters, and otherwise it is the result for the bound $f - 1$ and the word $\tau_k(w)$. Thus $\tau_k$ is applied to $w$ until the word has more than $n$ letters, at most $f$ times.

results.title: Letter counts in the Hofstadter word
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $x_k$ be the fixed point, starting with $k$, of the substitution sending the letter $k$ to $k\,1$ and every other letter $i$ to $i + 1$, and write $x_k[j]$ for its letter at index $j$. results.title: Numerical radius
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The numerical radius of a bounded linear operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space $H$ is the real number $w(T) = \sup \{ |\langle T x, x \rangle| : x \in H,\ \|x\| = 1 \}$, the supremum of the moduli of the values $\langle T x, x \rangle$ over the unit vectors of $H$ (taken to be $0$ when $H = 0$).

results.title: Real Cartesian part of an operator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a bounded linear operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space with adjoint $T^*$, the real Cartesian part of $T$ is the bounded linear operator $(T + T^*)/2$.

results.title: Imaginary Cartesian part of an operator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a bounded linear operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space with adjoint $T^*$, the imaginary Cartesian part of $T$ is the bounded linear operator $(T - T^*)/(2i)$.

results.title: The numerical-radius family is bounded above
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex inner product space $H$. The set $\{|\langle Tx, x\rangle| : x \in H,\ \|x\| = 1\}$ is bounded above.

results.title: Nonnegativity of the numerical radius
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every bounded operator $T$ on a complex inner product space, the numerical radius $w(T)$ of $T$ satisfies $w(T) \ge 0$.

results.title: The numerical radius bounds the quadratic form on unit vectors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex inner product space $H$, with numerical radius $w(T)$. For every $x \in H$ with $\|x\| = 1$, $|\langle Tx, x\rangle| \le w(T)$.

results.title: Bounding the numerical radius from above
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded operator on a complex inner product space $H$ and let $c \ge 0$ be a real number. If $|\langle T x, x\rangle| \le c$ for every unit vector $x \in H$, then the numerical radius of $T$ satisfies $w(T) \le c$.

results.title: Numerical radius at most the operator norm
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every bounded operator $T$ on a complex inner product space, the numerical radius $w(T)$ is at most the operator norm: $w(T) \le \|T\|$.

results.title: Quadratic form at the normalized vector
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded operator on a complex inner product space $H$. For every $x \in H$, $\langle T(\|x\|^{-1} x), \|x\|^{-1} x \rangle = \|x\|^{-2} \langle T x, x \rangle$, where $0^{-1}$ is read as $0$, so that for $x = 0$ both sides vanish.

results.title: Normalizing a nonzero vector gives a unit vector
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x$ be a nonzero vector in a complex inner product space. Then the vector $\|x\|^{-1} x$ has norm $1$.

results.title: Numerical radius bounds the normalized real part of the quadratic form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex inner product space $H$, with numerical radius $w(T)$. For every $x \in H$, $|\operatorname{Re} \langle Tx, x\rangle| / \|x\|^2 \le w(T)$, where division by zero is taken to be $0$, so the case $x = 0$ is trivial.

results.title: Numerical radius bounds the normalized imaginary part of the quadratic form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex inner product space $H$, with numerical radius $w(T)$. For every $x \in H$, $|\operatorname{Im} \langle Tx, x\rangle| / \|x\|^2 \le w(T)$, where division by zero is taken to be $0$, so the case $x = 0$ is trivial.

results.title: Numerical radius bounds the Rayleigh quotient
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex inner product space $H$, with numerical radius $w(T)$. For every $x \in H$, the Rayleigh quotient $R_T(x) = \operatorname{Re} \langle Tx, x\rangle / \|x\|^2$, taken to be $0$ at $x = 0$, satisfies $|R_T(x)| \le w(T)$.

results.title: Complex conjugate of one half
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The complex conjugate of $1/2 \in \mathbb{C}$ is $1/2$, that is, $\overline{1/2} = 1/2$.

results.title: Complex conjugate of minus half the imaginary unit
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The complex conjugate of $-i/2 \in \mathbb{C}$ is $i/2$, that is, $\overline{-i/2} = i/2$.

results.title: The real Cartesian part is symmetric
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every bounded linear operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space $H$ with adjoint $T^*$, the real Cartesian part $A = (T + T^*)/2$ is symmetric: $\langle Ax, y\rangle = \langle x, Ay\rangle$ for all $x, y \in H$.

results.title: The imaginary Cartesian part is symmetric
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every bounded linear operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space $H$ with adjoint $T^*$, the imaginary Cartesian part $B = (T - T^*)/(2i)$ is symmetric: $\langle Bx, y\rangle = \langle x, By\rangle$ for all $x, y \in H$.

results.title: Quadratic form of the real Cartesian part
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space $H$ and let $A = (T + T^*)/2$ be the real Cartesian part of $T$. Then for every $x \in H$ one has $\langle A x, x \rangle = \operatorname{Re} \langle T x, x \rangle$.

results.title: Quadratic form of the imaginary Cartesian part
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space $H$, whose inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is conjugate-linear in its first argument, and let $B = (T - T^*)/(2i)$ be the imaginary Cartesian part of $T$. Then for every $x \in H$ one has $\langle B x, x \rangle = -\operatorname{Im} \langle T x, x \rangle$.

results.title: Cartesian decomposition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every bounded linear operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space satisfies $T = A + iB$, where $A = (T + T^*)/2$ and $B = (T - T^*)/(2i)$ are the real and imaginary Cartesian parts of $T$ and $T^*$ is the adjoint of $T$.

results.title: Norm of the real part is at most the numerical radius
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space, with adjoint $T^*$, and let $A = (T + T^*)/2$ be its real Cartesian part. Then $\|A\| \le w(T)$, where $\|A\|$ is the operator norm of $A$ and $w(T)$ is the numerical radius of $T$.

results.title: Norm of the imaginary part is at most the numerical radius
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space, with adjoint $T^*$, and let $B = (T - T^*)/(2i)$ be its imaginary Cartesian part. Then $\|B\| \le w(T)$, where $\|B\|$ is the operator norm of $B$ and $w(T)$ is the numerical radius of $T$.

results.title: Operator norm at most twice the numerical radius
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every bounded operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space, $\|T\| \le 2\,w(T)$, where $\|T\|$ is the operator norm and $w(T)$ is the numerical radius of $T$.

results.title: Numerical radius of a self-adjoint operator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $T$ is a self-adjoint bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space, then its numerical radius equals its operator norm: $w(T) = \|T\|$.

results.title: The quadratic form of the adjoint has the same modulus
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space $H$, with adjoint $T^*$. For every $x \in H$, $|\langle T^* x, x\rangle| = |\langle T x, x\rangle|$, since $\langle T^* x, x\rangle$ is the complex conjugate of $\langle T x, x\rangle$.

results.title: Numerical radius of the adjoint
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every bounded operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space, the numerical radius of its adjoint $T^*$ equals the numerical radius of $T$: $w(T^*) = w(T)$.

results.title: Numerical range
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Forward orbit
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a self-map $f$ of a set $X$ and a point $x \in X$, the forward orbit of $x$ under $f$ is the set $\{f^n(x) : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ of all iterates of $x$, including $f^0(x) = x$.

results.title: Preperiodic point
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A point $x$ is preperiodic for a self-map $f$ when its forward orbit $\{f^n(x) : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ under $f$ is a finite set.

results.title: Strictly preperiodic point
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A point $x$ is strictly preperiodic for a self-map $f$ when it is preperiodic for $f$ but not periodic, that is, there is no $n > 0$ with $f^n(x) = x$.

results.title: Preperiodic point of a given type
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f$ be a self-map of a set $X$ and let $m$ and $n$ be natural numbers. A point $x \in X$ is preperiodic of type $(m, n)$ when $n > 0$ and $f^{m+n}(x) = f^m(x)$, that is, $f^m(x)$ is periodic with period $n$. Neither $m$ nor $n$ is required to be minimal.

results.title: Grand orbit relation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a self-map $f$ of a set $X$, points $x, y \in X$ are related, that is, lie in the same grand orbit of $f$, when $f^m(x) = f^n(y)$ for some natural numbers $m$ and $n$.

results.title: Grand orbit equivalence relation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a self-map $f$ of a set $X$, the relation on $X$ in which $x \sim y$ when $f^m(x) = f^n(y)$ for some natural numbers $m$ and $n$ is an equivalence relation; its equivalence classes are the grand orbits of $f$.

results.title: Grand orbit
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a self-map $f$ of a set $X$ and a point $x \in X$, the grand orbit of $x$ is the set of all $y \in X$ such that $f^m(x) = f^n(y)$ for some natural numbers $m$ and $n$, that is, the equivalence class of $x$ under the grand orbit relation.

results.title: ε-light vertex sets

results.title: Instances of resource-constrained project scheduling
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An instance of resource-constrained project scheduling (an RCPSP instance) is a quadruple $(J, P, C, D)$: a list $J$ of jobs, each a pair $(p, r) \in \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$ of a duration $p$ and a resource demand $r$; a list $P$ of precedence pairs $(a, b) \in \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$ of job indices; a resource capacity $C \in \mathbb{N}$; and a deadline $D \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: Resource-constrained project scheduling as a decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: RESOURCE-CONSTRAINED PROJECT SCHEDULING is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of RCPSP instances, to an RCPSP instance that is well formed and feasible. results.title: RESOURCE-CONSTRAINED PROJECT SCHEDULING is NP-complete

results.title: The class Δₙ of the arithmetical hierarchy
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number. A set $P$ of natural numbers is in $\Delta_n$ when it is in both classes $\Sigma_n$ and $\Pi_n$ of the arithmetical hierarchy.

results.title: Computable predicates are closed under computable precomposition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $P$ is a decidable set of natural numbers and $g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is a computable function, then the set $\{w \in \mathbb{N} : g(w) \in P\}$ is decidable.

results.title: The first projection of the pairing function is computable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\langle a, b \rangle$ denote the pairing bijection $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, $\langle a, b \rangle = b^2 + a$ if $a < b$ and $\langle a, b \rangle = a^2 + a + b$ otherwise. The function sending $z \in \mathbb{N}$ to the first component $a$ of the unique pair $(a, b)$ with $\langle a, b \rangle = z$ is computable.

results.title: The second projection of the pairing function is computable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\langle a, b \rangle$ denote the pairing bijection $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, $\langle a, b \rangle = b^2 + a$ if $a < b$ and $\langle a, b \rangle = a^2 + a + b$ otherwise. The function sending $z \in \mathbb{N}$ to the second component $b$ of the unique pair $(a, b)$ with $\langle a, b \rangle = z$ is computable.

results.title: The pairing function is computable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The pairing bijection $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle : \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, given by $\langle a, b \rangle = b^2 + a$ if $a < b$ and $\langle a, b \rangle = a^2 + a + b$ otherwise, is a computable function of its two arguments.

results.title: Computable predicates are closed under precomposition with pairing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\langle a, b \rangle$ denote the pairing bijection $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, $\langle a, b \rangle = b^2 + a$ if $a < b$ and $\langle a, b \rangle = a^2 + a + b$ otherwise. If $Q$ is a decidable set of natural numbers, then the set of pairs $(a, b) \in \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$ with $\langle a, b \rangle \in Q$ is decidable.

results.title: The hierarchy is closed under computable precomposition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be computable. If a set $P$ of natural numbers is in the class $\Sigma_n$ of the arithmetical hierarchy, then so is $\{w \in \mathbb{N} : g(w) \in P\}$; and if $P$ is in the class $\Pi_n$, then so is $\{w \in \mathbb{N} : g(w) \in P\}$.

results.summary: For every natural number $n$, writing $\Sigma_n$ and $\Pi_n$ for the classes of the arithmetical hierarchy, every $\Sigma_n$ set of natural numbers is in $\Sigma_{n+1}$ and every $\Pi_n$ set of natural numbers is in $\Pi_{n+1}$.

results.title: Σ₁ is the class of recursively enumerable predicates
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A predicate $P$ on $\mathbb{N}$ is recursively enumerable if and only if it is in $\Sigma_1$, that is, if and only if there is a computable predicate $Q$ on $\mathbb{N}$ such that for all $x$, $P(x)$ holds iff $Q(\langle x, y \rangle)$ holds for some $y$, where $\langle x, y \rangle$ is the standard pairing function of $\mathbb{N}$.

results.title: Graph codes
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A graph code consists of a vertex count $n \in \mathbb{N}$, with vertices $0, \dots, n-1$, and a Boolean adjacency matrix $A$ on these vertices that is symmetric ($A_{ij} = A_{ji}$ for all $i, j$) and loop-free ($A_{ii}$ is false for every $i$).

results.title: Binary digits of a natural number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The binary digits of $n \in \mathbb{N}$, most significant first, as a list of bits with the digit $1$ read as true and $0$ as false; for $n = 0$ this is the single digit $0$.

results.title: Prefix-free encoding of a natural number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The prefix-free encoding of $n \in \mathbb{N}$ consists of $k$ true bits, where $k$ is the number of binary digits of $n$, then one false bit, then the binary digits of $n$, most significant first.

results.title: Bit encoding of a graph code
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The bit encoding of a graph code with $n$ vertices and adjacency matrix $A$ is the prefix-free encoding of $n$ followed by the $n^2$ entries of $A$, as bits, in row-major order: $A_{0,0}, A_{0,1}, \dots, A_{0,n-1}, A_{1,0}, \dots, A_{n-1,n-1}$.

results.title: Bit encoding of a pair of graph codes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The bit encoding of a pair $(G, H)$ of graph codes is the bit encoding of $G$ followed by the bit encoding of $H$.

results.title: Isomorphism of graph codes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Graph codes $G$ and $H$ with adjacency matrices $A$ and $B$ are isomorphic when they have the same vertex count $n$ and there is a permutation $\sigma$ of the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that $A_{ij} = B_{\sigma(i)\sigma(j)}$ for all $i, j$.

results.title: Group exponentiation with modular exponents
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group, $q$ a natural number, $g \in G$ and $a \in \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$. Then $g^a$ is defined as $g^n$, where $n$ is the natural-number value of $a$: its representative in $\{0, \dots, q-1\}$ when $q > 0$, and $|a|$ when $q = 0$ (in which case $\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z} = \mathbb{Z}$).

results.title: Correctness of Diffie–Hellman key agreement
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group, $q$ a natural number and $g \in G$. Then $(g^b)^a = (g^a)^b$ for all $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: Exponentiation from a generator is a bijection
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group of order $q$, with $q \neq 0$, and let $g \in G$ generate $G$, that is, every element of $G$ is an integer power of $g$. Then $a \mapsto g^a$ is a bijection from $\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ to $G$, where $g^a = g^n$ for the representative $n \in \{0, \dots, q-1\}$ of $a$. Its inverse is the discrete logarithm to base $g$.
